account:
It is just after eleven on day 0. I have been keeping my morning appointments and walking the market, listening for news. Several townsfolk have repeated that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That is the only concrete report I have heard about town business; it could simply be normal baking supplies, and I have no evidence of anything unusual behind it. Freight was heading east across the bridge carrying an emerald. I tried calling to ask about trade, but apparently freight did not hear me, so I learned nothing about that business.

The unresolved matter is my three o'clock appointment: tea with 'the neighbour' at a dockside cottage on the east bank. The appointment book gives neither the host's name nor the particular cottage. The secretary has the book safely, says no correspondence has arrived, and promised to investigate the tea arrangements. I have now seen neighbour crossing westward at the bridge and am trying to get close enough to ask about tea directly. I suspect the tea entry may refer to this person, but that is not confirmed. Its stated purpose is a social visit; I do not yet know of any other purpose or any concealed gathering. My feeling that something is happening without me remains only a feeling, not an established fact. I still need to be home for noon lunch, back at the office for accounts at one, and at the correct dockside cottage at three.
